items.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: According to this marvelous book by Barry Singer, Alive At the Village Vanguard, which you claim as your memoir

ctx.x: He says so. I thought he was two. He keeps insisting it was three.
Ok. According to this marvelous book by Barry Singer, Alive At the Village Vanguard, which you claim as your memoir, you credit Phil with perhaps introducing you to jazz.

Not really. No one introduces you to anything. You listen. If you like it, you accept it. I mean, if you look at art and you like the painting, you say, “That’s it; I like that; I’ll collect some.” Or for anything. He didn’t, no. But we liked it together. I liked to share... Well, of course he was older than me, so maybe he knew something I didn’t know at the time. That’s quite possible. But I accepted it as a fait d’accompli. I loved it, and I’m glad he was there to be with me through all our jazz life, which…
